trial_title: Effect of Duodenal Mucosal Resurfacing (DMR) Using the Revita System in the Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes

inclusion_criteria.text: Diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes and evidence of preserved insulin secretion. Fasting insulin > 7.0 µU/mL.
Currently taking one or more oral glucose lowering medications, of which one must be Metformin, with no changes in medication in the previous 12 weeks prior to study entry
Able to comply with study requirements and understand and sign the informed consent

exclusion_criteria.text: Diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes or with a history of ketoacidosis
Current use of Insulin
Current use of GLP-1 analogues
Hypoglycemia unawareness or a history of severe hypoglycemia (more than 1 severe hypoglycemic event, as defined by need for third-party-assistance, in the last year)

Known autoimmune disease, as evidenced by a positive Anti-GAD test, including Celiac disease, or pre-existing symptoms of systemic lupus erythematosus, scleroderma or other autoimmune connective tissue disorder
Active H.pylori infection (Participants with active H. pylori may continue with the screening process if they are treated via medication)
Previous GI surgery that could affect the ability to treat the duodenum such as subjects who have had a Bilroth 2, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, or other similar procedures or conditions
History of chronic or acute pancreatitis
Known active hepatitis or active liver disease
Symptomatic gallstones or kidney stones, acute cholecystitis or history of duodenal inflammatory diseases including Crohn's Disease and Celiac Disease
History of coagulopathy, upper gastro-intestinal bleeding conditions such as ulcers, gastric varices, strictures, congenital or acquired intestinal telangiectasia
Use of anticoagulation therapy (such as warfarin) which cannot be discontinued for 7 days before and 14 days after the procedure
Use of P2Y12 inhibitors (clopidogrel, pasugrel, ticagrelor) which cannot be discontinued for 14 days before and 14 days after the procedure. Use of aspirin is allowed.
Unable to discontinue NSAIDs (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) during treatment through 4 weeks post procedure phase
Taking corticosteroids or drugs known to affect GI motility (e.g. Metoclopramide)
Receiving weight loss medications such as Meridia, Xenical, or over the counter weight loss medications
Persistent Anemia, defined as Hgb<10 g/dl
eGFR or MDRD <30 ml/min/1.73m2
Active systemic infection
Active malignancy within the last 5 years
Not potential candidates for surgery or general anesthesia
Active illicit substance abuse or alcoholism
Participating in another ongoing clinical trial of an investigational drug or device
Any other mental or physical condition which, in the opinion of the Investigator, makes the subject a poor candidate for clinical trial participation
HbA1c post run-in phase < 7.5% (59 mmol/mol) or > 10.0% (86 mmol/mol)

One or more Clinically significant hypoglycemic events defined as self-monitored or laboratory plasma glucose level of < 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L), or a severe hypoglycemic event requiring third-party-assistance, since the screening visit (Visit 1)

Hyperglycemic event defined as three self-monitored finger sticks in 1 day during the run-in period with fasting blood glucose measurements >15 mmol/L (270 mg/dL) or non-fasting blood glucose measurements >20 mmol/L (360 mg/dL)
Those who are pregnant, nursing or expect to become pregnant over the course of the study
Active and uncontrolled GERD defined as grade III esophagitis or greater
Abnormalities of the GI tract preventing endoscopic access to the duodenum
Anatomic abnormalities in the duodenum that would preclude the completion of the DMR procedure, including tortuous anatomy
Malignancy newly diagnosed by endoscopy
Upper gastro-intestinal conditions such as ulcers, polyps, gastric varices, strictures, congenital or acquired intestinal telangiectasia

visits.text: Visit 2: Baseline (Post Medication Run-In), 4-6 weeks after screening
Visit 2A: Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitor Return
Visit 7A: Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitor Return
Visit 3C: Cross-over to DMR Visit (0-14 days from Visit 9)

procedures.text: Demographics, medical history and full physical exam
Subject self-monitored blood glucose (SMBG) and glycemia diary
Liver MRI: Magnetic Resonance-Proton Density Fat Fraction (MR-PDFF) and Magnetic Resonance Liver Iron Content (MR-LIC)
Endoscopic evaluation of the esophagus, stomach and duodenum
Randomization 1:1 to DMR procedure or sham procedure
Duodenal Mucosal Resurfacing (DMR) procedure using the Revita System
Sham procedure: Revita catheter placed in the stomach for 30 minutes and removed

safety_information.text: AEs are collected from the time the Informed Consent is signed.
Glucose alert value <70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L): sufficiently low for treatment with fast-acting carbohydrate
